answer.rationale: No admissible measured evidence decides the criterion.

The claim is a physically reliable relaxed-configuration energy ranking across four sampled Cantor FCC arrangements. The evidence does not decide it, and I see no basis for calling it contradicted either. The only admissible numbers are two converged static single points. Ideal (MATS-0080) is -7.828097 eV/atom and random1 (MATS-0081) is -7.827905 eV/atom, so ideal is lower by 0.192 meV/atom (ev-5ba7f0eadd904a0add85056c). That ordering is a finite-mesh static ordering only, and the arithmetic record itself says it is not a qualified relaxed-configuration ranking. Several gaps keep it from supporting the claim. (1) The relaxations for ideal and random1 are not_converged because ionic-step SCF cycles hit NELM (ev-47538e8e8ffb560efba09b7b, ev-a6ae516463066bcf748458cd). Under the rules these records count neither for nor against the ranking. The static geometries are therefore not qualified relaxed structures. (2) The random1 static has a residual max force of 0.466 eV/A (ev-9c17747679a6fc7e543fa258). That is far from relaxed and well above the 0.02 target, while the ideal static is at 0.012 eV/A (ev-54ffb0964eab50c0a8461805). The two energies are therefore not comparable at matched relaxation quality. Relaxing random1 would lower its energy by an unknown amount. That amount could plausibly be comparable to or larger than the 0.19 meV/atom gap, and could even reverse the order. (3) Random1's static total moment is 63.78 muB against 62.22 muB at the end of its relaxation, which indicates a different electronic and magnetic solution. With a single collinear initialization and one 2x2x2 Gamma mesh, magnetic and k-point uncertainty is unbounded and probably exceeds 0.19 meV/atom. (4) Random2 failed on walltime with 0.169 eV/A residual force and no static (ev-b5f9de910d86bf461b725bcf). Random3 failed with an MPI error and no static (ev-bea28ffbd28caf685397e4a9). Two of the four configurations are therefore absent from any ranking. A DFT follow-up could decide the claim. It would qualify the ionic relaxations, run matched denser-k statics on the closest qualified pair, and test an alternative magnetic initialization. This is the scope_gap test. I have no peer claims to dispute yet. I would challenge any peer who treats the 0.19 meV/atom static ordering as a ranking of relaxed configurations.

answer.rationale:
My verdict is unresolved. The claim is not supported, and the evidence does not contradict it either.

Supported points:
- Two static single points converged. Ideal MATS-0080 is at -7.828097 eV/atom and random1 MATS-0081 is at -7.827905 eV/atom, so ideal is lower by 0.192 meV/atom (ev-54ffb0964eab50c0a8461805, ev-9c17747679a6fc7e543fa258, ev-5ba7f0eadd904a0add85056c).
- That is only a finite-mesh static ordering of two geometries. The ranking record itself says it is "not a qualified relaxed-configuration ranking."

Why the claim is not supported:
- Both preceding relaxations are not_converged because of SCF cap hits at NELM=200 (ev-47538e8e8ffb560efba09b7b, ev-a6ae516463066bcf748458cd). Under the rules these records are not evidence either way, so the static geometries have no qualified relaxed provenance.
- Random2 was killed by walltime and random3 failed with an MPI error (ev-b5f9de910d86bf461b725bcf, ev-bea28ffbd28caf685397e4a9). Neither has a static result, so at most two of the four arrangements are covered.
- Random1 static has a 0.466 eV/A max force. Its relaxation reported 0.0178 eV/A at an identical geometry hash, and its total moment shifted from 62.22 to 63.78 muB. Peer arguments that this is simply a poor geometry are only partly right. A different electronic or magnetic solution is at least as plausible, and the records do not distinguish the two.
- The 0.192 meV/atom gap is about 21 meV per cell. That is the same order as plausible errors from the residual force, the single 2x2x2 Gamma mesh with sigma=0.1 eV, and the single MAGMOM start. No uncertainties are recorded.
- On the dispute between peers over how large the force-related error is: I agree with claude-sonnet's second-round point that it is unbounded by the records. It is neither shown to be larger than the gap nor shown to be smaller. I would not accept gemini-flash's flat statement that the gap is "well within typical uncertainty" as established.

Why not contradicted: no admissible records disagree. The ideal-lower static ordering is not refuted, only unqualified.

Decisive test: the scope_gap option. Requalify the ideal and random1 relaxations with no SCF-capped ionic steps. Then run matched denser-k-mesh statics on that pair plus one alternative collinear magnetic initialization. The pair ordering holds only if its sign persists and exceeds the spread across mesh and magnetic start. Random2 and random3 would need qualified relaxations and statics before any four-way ranking. DFT could decide this, so I request it.
